hand.title: Daily Hand

events.text: You raised before the cards were dealt. Your opponent called.
Flop — 4, 4, Queen. You bet. Your opponent raised you back.
Turn — Ace. Your opponent bet out. You called.

wrongReasons: K 4 plays similarly, but the correct hand pairs a specific board card that K 4 doesn't. Look at which hole card ranks actually appear on the board.
With only two pair, Q 5 wouldn't commit chips across multiple streets. This betting line requires a genuinely made hand from the flop onward.
With only one pair, 6 K wouldn't commit chips across multiple streets. This betting line requires a genuinely made hand from the flop onward.
hand.explanation:
Answer: 4 10

Your opponent flopped three of a kind and raised the flop immediately to build the pot. Sets are too strong to slow-play — they pushed their advantage on every street.
